question: What new school structure does the policy propose to replace the 10+2 structure, and which ages does it cover?
expected_answer: A 5+3+3+4 curricular and pedagogical structure covering ages 3-18.

evidence.text: 5+3+3+4 covering ages 3-18

question: What are the four stages of the 5+3+3+4 design, with their grades and ages?
expected_answer: Foundational (3 years of Anganwadi/pre-school + Grades 1-2, ages 3-8), Preparatory (Grades 3-5, ages 8-11), Middle (Grades 6-8, ages 11-14), Secondary (Grades 9-12, ages 14-18).

evidence.text: Preparatory Stage (Grades 3-5, covering ages 8-11), Middle Stage (Grades 6-8, covering ages 11-14)

question: What percentage of a child's cumulative brain development occurs before the age of 6?
expected_answer: Over 85%.

evidence.text: cumulative brain development occurs prior to the age of 6

question: By what year must universal quality early childhood care and education be achieved?
expected_answer: As soon as possible, and no later than 2030.

evidence.text: no later than 2030, to ensure that all students entering Grade 1 are school ready

question: Who will develop the National Curricular and Pedagogical Framework for ECCE, and for which age group?
expected_answer: NCERT will develop it for children up to the age of 8, in two parts: a sub-framework for 0-3 year-olds and one for 3-8 year-olds.

evidence.text: for children up to the age of 8 will be developed by NCERT in two parts

question: What training will Anganwadi workers with 10+2 qualifications versus lower qualifications receive?
expected_answer: Those with 10+2 and above get a 6-month certificate programme in ECCE; those with lower qualifications get a one-year diploma programme.

evidence.text: 6-month certificate programme in ECCE; and those with lower educational qualifications shall be given a one-year diploma programme

question: By when is universal foundational literacy and numeracy to be achieved in primary school?
expected_answer: By 2025 (every student attaining it by Grade 3).

evidence.text: universal foundational literacy and numeracy in primary school by 2025

question: Roughly how many elementary school students have not attained foundational literacy and numeracy?
expected_answer: Over 5 crore.

evidence.text: estimated to be over 5 crore in number

question: What pupil-teacher ratio will be ensured at the level of each school, and what is the aim for areas with many disadvantaged students?
expected_answer: Under 30:1 for each school; under 25:1 for areas with large numbers of socio-economically disadvantaged students.

evidence.text: PTR) of under 30:1 will be ensured at the level of each school

question: What were the Gross Enrolment Ratios for Grades 6-8, 9-10 and 11-12 cited in the policy?
expected_answer: 90.9% for Grades 6-8, 79.3% for Grades 9-10, and 56.5% for Grades 11-12.

evidence.text: The GER for Grades 6-8 was 90.9%, while for Grades 9-10 and 11-12 it was only 79.3% and 56.5%, respectively

question: How many out-of-school children aged 6 to 17 did the 2017-18 NSSO survey report?
expected_answer: 3.22 crore.

evidence.text: number of out of school children in the age group of 6 to 17 years is 3.22 crore

question: What Gross Enrolment Ratio goal is set for preschool to secondary level, and by when?
expected_answer: 100% GER in preschool to secondary level by 2030.

evidence.text: 100% Gross Enrolment Ratio in preschool to secondary level by 2030

question: Until which grade should the medium of instruction be the home language or mother tongue?
expected_answer: At least until Grade 5, but preferably till Grade 8 and beyond.

evidence.text: the medium of instruction until at least Grade 5, but preferably till Grade 8 and beyond

question: What condition applies to the three languages students learn under the three-language formula?
expected_answer: The three languages are chosen by States, regions and students, so long as at least two of the three are native to India; no language is imposed on any State.

evidence.text: so long as at least two of the three languages are native to India

question: How long is the bagless period all students will take during Grades 6-8?
expected_answer: 10 days, during which they intern with local vocational experts.

evidence.text: All students will participate in a 10-day bagless period sometime during Grades 6-8

question: How many times in a school year will students be allowed to take Board Exams?
expected_answer: Up to two occasions: one main examination and one for improvement.

evidence.text: allowed to take Board Exams on up to two occasions during any given school year

question: In which grades will all students take school examinations, apart from Board exams in Grades 10 and 12?
expected_answer: Grades 3, 5 and 8.

evidence.text: all students will take school examinations in Grades 3, 5, and 8

question: What does PARAKH stand for?
expected_answer: Performance Assessment, Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development - the proposed National Assessment Centre.

evidence.text: National Assessment Centre, PARAKH (Performance Assessment, Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development)

question: How many hours of continuous professional development is each teacher expected to complete every year?
expected_answer: At least 50 hours.

evidence.text: Each teacher will be expected to participate in at least 50 hours of CPD

question: What will be the minimum degree qualification for teaching by 2030?
expected_answer: A 4-year integrated B.Ed. degree.

evidence.text: By 2030, the minimum degree qualification for teaching will be a 4-year integrated B.Ed.

question: What fund will the Government of India constitute for girls and transgender students?
expected_answer: A 'Gender-Inclusion Fund'.

evidence.text: Gender-Inclusion Fund

question: What is a school complex as described in the policy?
expected_answer: A grouping of one secondary school together with all other schools offering lower grades in its neighbourhood, including Anganwadis, within a radius of five to ten kilometers.

evidence.text: consisting of one secondary school together with all other schools offering lower grades in its neighbourhood including Anganwadis, in a radius of five to ten kilometers

question: What does SSSA stand for and what is its role?
expected_answer: State School Standards Authority - an independent State-wide body that sets minimal standards (safety, security, infrastructure, teachers, financial probity, governance) for all schools.

evidence.text: State School Standards Authority (SSSA)

question: What higher education GER target does the policy set, and by when?
expected_answer: Raise GER from 26.3% (2018) to 50% by 2035.

question: Over how many years will the affiliated colleges system be phased out?
expected_answer: Over a period of fifteen years, through graded autonomy.

evidence.text: over a period of fifteen years through a system of graded autonomy

question: How long is the undergraduate degree, and what exit certifications are offered?
expected_answer: 3 or 4 years (4-year preferred), with a certificate after 1 year, a diploma after 2 years, and a Bachelor's degree after 3 years.

evidence.text: The undergraduate degree will be of either 3 or 4-year duration, with multiple exit options

question: What is the Academic Bank of Credit?
expected_answer: A system that digitally stores the academic credits earned from various recognized HEIs, so degrees can be awarded taking those credits into account.

evidence.text: An Academic Bank of Credit (ABC) shall be established which would digitally store

question: What happens to the M.Phil. programme under the policy?
expected_answer: It will be discontinued.

question: What does the policy propose to rename the Ministry of Human Resource Development?
expected_answer: Ministry of Education (MoE).

evidence.text: be re-designated as the Ministry of Education (MoE)

question: What is the National Educational Technology Forum (NETF)?
expected_answer: An autonomous body to be created as a platform for exchanging ideas on using technology to enhance learning, assessment, planning and administration in school and higher education.

evidence.text: An autonomous body, the National Educational Technology Forum (NETF), will be created

question: What decade will the entire policy be in operational mode, after which another comprehensive review is planned?

evidence.text: In the decade of 2030-40, the entire policy will be in an operational mode

question: What are the four verticals of the Higher Education Commission of India (HECI) and the function of each?
expected_answer: NHERC (regulation), NAC (accreditation), HEGC (funding), and GEC (academic standard setting / learning outcomes).

evidence.text: These four structures will be set up as four independent verticals within one umbrella institution, the Higher Education Commission of India (HECI)
The third vertical of HECI will be the Higher Education Grants Council (HEGC)

question: By which year does the policy target 100% GER from preschool to secondary, and by which year 50% GER in higher education?
expected_answer: 100% GER in preschool to secondary by 2030; 50% GER in higher education by 2035.

question: What is current public spending on education as a share of GDP versus the policy's target?

to reach 6% of GDP at the earliest

question: Which body develops the National Professional Standards for Teachers, by when, and when will they be reviewed?
